The facts of the case giving rise to the filing of appeal are that the marriage of appellant and complainant was solemnized on 8.12.2008 according to Hindu rites and customs and one child was born out of the wedlock namely Master Davesh / respondent no. 2.

It is also alleged that since the day of marriage, the behaviour of appellant and his family members was not good towards respondent no. 1 as they were not happy with the dowry articles given by the parents of respondent no. 1 and they taunted respondent no. 1 and pressurized her to bring more dowry.

sentences.text: To determine the quantum of maintenance/monetary relief, the only question for consideration is whether the quantum of maintenance awarded by Ld. Trial Court is just and does not call for interference.
The quantum of maintenance has to be decided on the basis of material on record.
The expression maintenance includes expenses for food, clothing, residence, medical and other expenses relating to normal pursuits of life.

Thus the needs and requirements of the wife for a moderate living, the earning of the husband, his capacity to earn are the relevant factors to be considered while determining the quantum of maintenance.
26. The factum of marriage is not disputed.

Appellant also stated that he did not know anything further about the declaration notice.
Thus, the contention of appellant that his father disowned him and he was residing in rented accommodation cannot be said to have been proved.

29. However, the Ld. Trial Court was rightly of the view that respondent no. 1 failed to show that the house no. D111 JJ Colony, Shiv Mandir, New Delhi was a shared household of the appellant and respondent no. 1.
In this regard, complainant had stated in her cross examination that the above said house was in the name of her father inlaw.
The complainant failed to bring on record any evidence to show that it was a joint family property in which her husband/appellant had a share.
Thus, Ld. trial court rightly declined the declared to above house as shared household.

sentences.text: The Ld. Trial Court was rightly of the view that in OPD of the appellant there was no mention of the fact of history of burning by respondent no. 1 by pouring kerosene oil or that the clothes of appellant were drenched with kerosene oil.
Moreover that OPD did not bear the stamp of doctor concerned.
Thus the appellant failed to prove that the respondent no. 1/complainant harassed him and tried to set him on fire.

I am of the view that the allegation of the appellant that respondent no. 1 tried to set him on fire stands falsified and the cruelty meted to respondent No.1 by appellant and his family stands substantiated.
31. For the foregoing reasons, I do not find any illegality in the impugned judgment.

I accordingly,

opennyai_summary.facts:
The Ld. Trial Court vide the impugned Judgment directed the appellant/husband to pay Rs. 10,000/ per month to the respondent/complainant and the child towards maintenance and alternative accommodation from the date of filing of complaint.
The respondents being aggrieved by the cruelty of appellant and his family members and as the appellant failed to make any provision for their livelihood filed a complaint u/s 12, 18, 19, 20 & 22 of the Act.
The Ld. Trial Court after considering the pleadings, evidence and documents held that it was the duty of the appellant to maintain the respondent no.1 who was his legally wedded wife and his child/respondent no. 2 and vide impugned judgment directed the appellant to pay Rs.10000/
per month as maintenance to the respondents which included the maintenance for alternative accommodation.
opennyai_summary.arguments: It was denied that respondents levelled false allegations of cruelty meted out to her against appellant and his family members.

To determine the quantum of maintenance/monetary relief, the only question for consideration is whether the quantum of maintenance awarded by Ld. Trial Court is just and does not call for interference.
The quantum of maintenance has to be decided on the basis of material on record.
The expression maintenance includes expenses for food, clothing, residence, medical and other expenses relating to normal pursuits of life.
Thus the needs and requirements of the wife for a moderate living, the earning of the husband, his capacity to earn are the relevant factors to be considered while determining the quantum of maintenance.
